overall_summary: Analysis of 47 deduplicated Shorts reveals a stark performance divide: first-person experiential 'What If You Fell Into...' exoplanet scenarios and extreme planetary anomalies dominate channel traffic (generating 700 to 1,055 views with strong engagement), whereas re-uploaded generic psychology facts (e.g., brain memory illusions) and static trivia languish below 60 views. In addition, videos optimized at 19-21 seconds consistently achieve peak viewership and engagement compared to shorter 12-16 second uploads.

winning_patterns.pattern: First-Person 'What If You Fell Into...' Visceral Cosmic Scenarios
winning_patterns.evidence: 'What If You Fell Into a Liquid Diamond Planet?' (1,029 views, 38 likes) and 'What If You Fell Into the Planet of Burning Ice?' (972 views, 18 likes) lead all uploads in reach and engagement.
winning_patterns.action: Double down on high-stakes, first-person what-if survival scenarios exploring extreme cosmic and planetary phenomena.

winning_patterns.evidence: Videos like 'The Planet Darker Than Coal: TrES-2b' (1,028 views, 36 likes) and 'Venus Has a Day Longer Than Its Year' (981 views, 21 likes) at 19-21s vastly outperformed sub-16s videos (averaging <100 views).
winning_patterns.action: Maintain runtime strictly between 19 and 21 seconds to maximize watch time without sacrificing completion rate.

weak_patterns.pattern: Generic Brain Psychology and Memory Factoids
weak_patterns.evidence: Multiple iterations of 'Your Brain Can Create Fake Memories' flatlined at 5, 10, and 53 views; 'Your Brain Is Hiding This From You' garnered only 38 views.
weak_patterns.action: Cease low-urgency psychology trivia unless framed through cinematic horror/micro-mystery narratives.

weak_patterns.evidence: Republishing 'Why Space Is Completely Silent' 3 times produced diminishing returns (dropping from 220 to 87 to 34 views).
weak_patterns.action: Enforce strict fresh-topic filters; never re-upload verbatim concept variations.
